newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks seen up despite central bank warning.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks seen up despite central bank warning.

text.p: Taiwan share prices are expected to be firmer but with limited gains on Thursday after the central bank urged investors to exercise "extra caution" when investing in the rallying stock market, brokers said.

Central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung warned on Wednesday that Taiwan's stock market turnover and price-earnings ratio were far higher than in other countries. "Investors should be risk-conscious and be extra careful. What the central bank can do has already been done," Hsu said without elaboration.
On Wednesday, the index ended up 195.19 points at a six-year high of 8,655.82. A 8,620-8,720 range was seen for Thursday.

"The central bank can now use only moral persuasion and open market operations (to slightly tighten liquidity), and that's not enough to stop the currently bullish sentiment," said Michael Hung, an independent senior analyst.
"The index should continue to test 9,000 in coming sessions, but the central bank warning would nevertheless trigger some caution to limit Thursday's gains," Hung said.
Financials are seen rising further as the Big Three state-run banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan -- will issue dividends on Thursday of T$5, T$5 and T$2 per share, respectively, he said.
